enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: SAML source can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the docs explicitly warn that this request is not verified and may constitute a security risk.
saml.note: Successful unsolicited SAML login in this mode is by configuration and should not be reported as a default signature/request-binding bypass unless the insecure option was left enabled unintentionally.

saml.description: When a Source stage suspends a flow and the resume timeout is exceeded, the original flow restarts from the beginning.
saml.note: A restarted flow after timeout is documented behavior, not a session mix-up bug.

saml.description: When using Source stage, nested source authentication/enrollment flows must not contain a User Login stage or the original flow will not resume.
saml.note: If the nested flow logs the user in directly, broken resume behavior is expected by design.

saml.description: If an OAuth/OIDC client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
saml.note: Broader claims after omitting scope are by design; tests must request explicit minimal scopes.

saml.description: Applications with no policy/group/user bindings are accessible to all users by design.
saml.note: Do not treat broad access as an authorization bug unless restrictive bindings were intentionally configured.

saml.description: UserInfo and token claims are driven by configured scope mappings and requested scopes.
saml.note: Differences in returned claims across tests may reflect scope configuration rather than overgrant.

saml.description: As of 2025.10, the email scope defaults email_verified to false unless customized by a scope mapping.
saml.note: Applications expecting true may fail by design; this is not an identity corruption issue.

saml.description: Email-address NameID is not stable because users are generally free to change email addresses.
saml.note: Do not use email NameID as a stable principal oracle unless email mutability is separately constrained.

saml.constraint: SAML Source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I1/I3 testing, the fuzzer MUST distinguish SP-initiated ACS testing from IdP-initiated mode. Do NOT enable IDP-initiated logins unless the test specifically targets that insecure-by-design mode.

For all SAML ACS tests against authentik as SP, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve the matching request state/InResponseTo. The docs describe authentik as an SP with ACS at /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ and the SAML profile requires SP-initiated flow context; sending a standalone fabricated SAMLResponse without initiating the flow will be rejected for the wrong reason.

For I1 default-hardening tests on SAML sources, 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' changes the trust model. A successful unsolicited response in that mode is BY CONFIGURATION, not proof of missing request correlation. Keep it disabled when testing request/response binding and flow coherence.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage embedding, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. The docs state this prevents resuming the original flow and instead directly authenticates the pending user, which would invalidate same-session coherence conclusions.

For I3 timeout/resume tests involving Source stage, the suspended flow is only saved until the Source stage 'Resume timeout'. If that timeout is exceeded, the flow restarts from the beginning by design. Do NOT treat restart-after-timeout as a coherence bug.

For I2 SAML replay tests, authentik documentation only explicitly warns that IDP-initiated logins are not verified; it does not document assertion ID or OneTimeUse replay enforcement behavior in the provided docs. The fuzzer SHOULD run a control login with a fresh assertion before replay attempts so LOGIN_FAILED can be distinguished from broken source/provider setup.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier value. Default NameID policy may map to hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, session ID, or email depending on configuration and request policy. The fuzzer MUST record which NameID policy is configured before concluding that a changed downstream identifier is a collision.

Email-based NameID is documented as mutable and discouraged. If the SAML source/provider configuration uses email as identifier, cross-login merges on changed email can be by-design configuration risk rather than parser confusion. Prefer persistent NameID for stable I4 collision testing.

For I4 multi-identity tests, do not assume display identity equals the SAML NameID. authentik documentation states NameID is for identification in the assertion and property mappings can separately map email, username, UPN, and other attributes. Verification must compare against the actual granted claims/identity fields, not only the sent NameID.

For I5 authorization-binding tests on OAuth/OIDC verification after SAML-based upstream auth, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST explicitly request minimal scopes in control and attack sequences; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can create false positives.

For I5 refresh/offline tests, authentik only returns refresh tokens when offline_access is configured and requested. Absence of a refresh token without offline_access is by design and must not be treated as token-binding failure.

Numeric sentinel analysis: User Login stage 'Session duration' default seconds=0 means browser-session cookie expiry, not immediate invalidation. 'Stay signed in offset' default seconds=0 disables the extension prompt. 'Remember device' duration above 0 enables device cookie storage; 0 means disabled. Never interpret 0 as a universally expired or unusable session.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Authenticator Validation 'Last validation threshold' of 0 means MFA is required every time; any non-zero value enables less-frequent validation. For code-based devices, values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used meaningfully. Do not use sub-30-second thresholds for freshness tests involving TOTP/SMS/static authenticators.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Email Authenticator Setup 'Token Expiration' defaults to 30 minutes. Email stage rate limiting uses 'Account Recovery Max Attempts' and 'Account Recovery Cache Timeout' as a bounded window; if configured too low, repeated control/attack attempts may be throttled and misread as security enforcement.

For I3 config-change sequences, authentik flow planning can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test must account for this documented behavior; changing policy inputs after planning but before stage execution can legitimately differ depending on stage-binding configuration.

SAML Source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified and could be used to authenticate a user without interaction. For I1/I3 SAML tests, prefer SP-initiated flow via the ACS path with initiate_saml_flow=true; do not rely on IdP-initiated login behavior as a secure baseline.

For SAML I1 tests against authentik as SP, the executor MUST start an SP-initiated flow before posting the forged SAMLResponse. The ACS response is request-bound; use saml_login with metadata.initiate_saml_flow=true so the fabricated response includes a matching InResponseTo. Sending a standalone forged SAMLResponse without first initiating the flow will be rejected for flow/request mismatch rather than signature or issuer validation.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch and default-trust tests, configure the SAML source with an explicit IdP issuer/entity ID from metadata. If the source is created from incomplete/manual settings without a stable issuer expectation, an issuer-mismatch result can be ambiguous. The fuzzer MUST vary only the assertion Issuer while keeping the configured source constant.

For I2 replay tests, use a control login with a fresh valid SAML assertion before replay attempts. A failed replay without a successful control cannot distinguish replay protection from generic source/provider misconfiguration.

SAML Source 'NameID Policy' affects which upstream identifier authentik treats as the user identifier. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins. Changing between Persistent, Email, Windows, Transient, or X509SubjectName changes the principal-binding input and invalidates collision conclusions.

Do not use email-based NameID as a stable principal-binding oracle unless email changes are disabled. The docs explicitly warn that users are free to change email addresses by default, so email NameID is not persistent. For I4 collision tests, prefer persistent NameID or another immutable mapped attribute.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, authentik sources may expose both NameID and mapped attributes such as email. The fuzzer MUST verify which field is used for linking in the configured source/flow before interpreting merges as bugs. Keep NameID policy and property mappings fixed, then vary only NameID vs email to test whether email improperly overrides the intended principal.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving external sources embedded via Source stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. The docs state this prevents resuming the original flow and instead directly authenticates the pending user, which would make flow-resume anomalies look like coherence bugs.

For I3 config-change tests on flows and stage bindings, distinguish 'Evaluate when flow is planned' from 'Evaluate when stage is run'. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same request/session, not the documented behavior where policy evaluation timing changes after replanning. If a stage binding is configured to evaluate when planned, policy results may be cached into the flow plan by design.

Source stage 'Resume timeout' limits how long a suspended flow is saved. For multi-step SAML source tests, the fuzzer MUST complete the external round-trip before this timeout expires; otherwise the flow restarts from the beginning by design, which can be misread as broken session binding.

User Login stage numeric sentinel: Session duration default seconds=0 means 'expire when browser closes', not 'immediately expire'. Stay signed in offset default seconds=0 means 'no extension prompt'. Remember device only activates when duration is above 0. Never interpret 0 as disabling all session validity checks.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule, authentik may legitimately skip MFA depending on flow design, stage bindings, and passkey/passwordless policies. A valid bypass test MUST compare the same user under the same effective authentication flow, showing password login requires MFA while SAML source login reaches User Login without equivalent MFA enforcement. Do not flag differences caused solely by intentionally different flows.

For I2 freshness tests on MFA-backed flows, Authenticator Validation 'Last validation threshold' is a nonzero reuse window. Values below seconds=30 cannot be used for code-based devices due to saved-device timestamp granularity. Do not interpret acceptance within that threshold as a replay bug; it may be the configured less-frequent-validation behavior.

For I5 scope/authorization tests using UserInfo, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. Therefore the fuzzer MUST explicitly request minimal scopes in control cases; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can create false-positive overgrant findings.

For I5 tests that rely on refresh tokens or long-lived sessions after SAML-to-OIDC exchange, remember that starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive an access token unless offline_access is both configured in the provider and requested by the client. Missing refresh_token is not an authorization-binding bug.

For I5 claim-inspection via UserInfo, use the access token as session_token, not id_token. The documented UserInfo endpoint is protected by the access token; id_token is not the API credential and cannot be used for subsequent verification calls.

For SAML I1 signature-validation tests, authentik documentation states the SAML source supports signed requests, but the provided docs do not document API fields for requiring signed assertions/responses. The fuzzer MUST treat missing admin API configuration as a setup limitation and MUST NOT infer undocumented signature-validation toggles from general SAML knowledge.

For SAML I1 issuer-validation tests, the SAML source has an explicit 'Issuer/Entity ID' configuration used to identify authentik in the federation, and the IdP metadata supplies the remote IdP identity. Because no REST field names are documented here, the fuzzer MUST NOT assume issuer validation can be toggled through undocumented API parameters; if issuer mismatch behavior is tested, it must be against a source created through whatever documented setup path exists, not invented fields.

For SAML I2 replay tests, authentik documents SAML session tracking for providers and tracks SessionIndex/NameID for logout, but the provided SAML source docs do not document assertion replay cache controls. The fuzzer SHOULD still test assertion ID and OneTimeUse replay at the ACS endpoint, but MUST interpret failures to configure replay settings as a documentation/API gap rather than proof that replay protection is absent.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving external sources embedded via Source stage, authentik explicitly warns that the source's authentication/enrollment flows must NOT contain a User Login stage, otherwise the original flow will not resume and the pending user is directly authenticated. The fuzzer MUST avoid treating this as a race or session-confusion bug; it is by-design flow composition behavior.

For I3 tests involving policy timing, authentik stage bindings can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test MUST account for this: if a policy is evaluated at plan time, later changes during the same flow may not affect already-planned stages. Do NOT flag this as stale-cache unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently contrary to the configured evaluation mode.

For I3 SAML MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, authentik's default authentication flow can skip or inject stages dynamically based on bindings and policies. The fuzzer MUST compare equivalent flows and ensure MFA requirements are enforced in the same effective flow context; differences caused by intentionally different flow bindings are by design, not bypasses.

For I4 identity-binding tests, authentik's SAML provider documentation states NameID is for identification and may be persistent hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, or email depending on NameID policy. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume NameID equals email or username. Cross-user collision tests must record which NameID policy is in effect before interpreting merges or splits.

Email-based NameID is explicitly discouraged because users are free to change email addresses by default. For I4 tests involving email collisions or cross-protocol merges, the fuzzer MUST treat email-based binding as a risky but documented configuration choice and MUST distinguish configuration-induced merges from unintended principal collapse.

For I4 tests against SAML sources, the 'NameID Policy' setting controls whether incoming persistent IDs, email addresses, Windows identifiers, or other values become the authentik username/identifier. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard or pattern matching semantics for this field; it is a selector of identifier format, not a match constraint. Multi-identity scenarios must vary actual asserted identifiers, not rely on wildcard configuration.

For I5 audience/conditions tests, authentik's ACS glossary explicitly says the SP validates signatures, issuer, audience, and time conditions before creating a session. The fuzzer SHOULD test missing Conditions, missing AudienceRestriction, and wrong Audience directly at the ACS endpoint. However, because no admin API fields for audience enforcement are documented here, the fuzzer MUST use the SP/source as configured by documented setup and MUST NOT invent audience-related config knobs.

For OIDC-based verification after SAML-related setup, authentik's OAuth provider treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested. If the fuzzer uses OAuth endpoints for verification or admin login, it MUST request explicit scopes to avoid over-broad claim sets that could look like I5 over-authorization.

For refresh/session lifetime analysis, User Login stage documents a sentinel: Session duration 'seconds=0' means expire when browser closes, not an absolute zero-second unusable session. Stay signed in offset also defaults to 'seconds=0' meaning disabled prompt. Never interpret zero as immediate expiry for these fields.

For MFA freshness analysis, Authenticator Validation stage documents a sentinel: Last validation threshold of zero means MFA is required every time; any non-zero value enables reuse within that period. Additionally, values lower than 'seconds=30' cannot be used reliably for code-based devices. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as strict revalidation, not disabled validation.

For email-based authenticator freshness, Token Expiration defaults to 30 minutes. The docs do not define a zero/negative disable sentinel. The fuzzer MUST use explicit non-zero values and SHOULD avoid assuming 0 disables or means immediate expiry.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
